evidence: Mechanical half (manual application of check-solve-contract.py; not the private checker): task/solution/solve.sh (sha256 1df2ed04...030a, 36 lines) has '#!/bin/bash' shebang, 0 CR bytes, passes 'bash -n'; set -euo pipefail; 'mkdir -p /app' then 'cp -a "$(dirname "$0")/app/." /app/' (line 34) installs the golden to /app as the template does; the only other writes are 'rm -f -- "$database_path" ...-wal ...-shm' (line 35) where database_path is realpath of ${DB_PATH:-/app/app.db} and is forced under /app (lines 5-9, exit 1 otherwise). No write to /tests, /logs/verifier or /solution; no pkill, no NODE_ENV, no npm/pip install, no bare nproc. The added Node preflight (lines 12-33) only reads /proc to refuse resetting a database that a live process holds open, and exits 0 immediately when no database file exists (line 16), i.e. on a fresh Oracle container. Runtime contract vs instruction.md/integration.md/hireops_rules.md s.8/test.sh: entry /app/server.js exists and requires src/index.js, which in the main thread starts bootstrap.js; bootstrap.js:43 listens on Number(process.env.PORT||3000) on 0.0.0.0 and answers GET/HEAD /api/health (bootstrap.js:20-23) before and independent of the SQLite worker, satisfying 'health never touches the database'; UI and API share the one process via a loopback proxy to the worker (bootstrap.js:28-41, index.js:447 listens 127.0.0.1:0). Worker gets {...process.env, PORT:'0'} so DB_PATH/NODE_PATH from test.sh's env -i launch (test.sh:104-111) are inherited; db.js:9 honours DB_PATH, default /app/app.db. Seed is read from src/seed_data.json beside the module (db.js:10), byte-identical to environment/assets/seed_data.json (both sha256 a1c65c80...3740), so /assets is not needed at runtime; UI served from path.join(__dirname,'..','public') (index.js:42) - no cwd assumption, matching rules s.8 (test.sh may launch /tmp/submission copy as uid 65534). Seeding is idempotent: seedIfEmpty returns when users count>0 and inserts inside one transaction (db.js:61-85). Dependencies are only express/better-sqlite3 via NODE_PATH (package.json pins 5.1.0/12.4.1, matching environment/Dockerfile global installs) plus node built-ins; index.html loads only local /styles.css and /js/*.js; client uses same-origin fetch and EventSource /api/events; no outbound server calls. No shipped app.db in solution/app. Runtime observation: raw-evidence-index entries re-hashed equal to current files and all 12 matching_source_files (incl. solve.sh) equal frozen bytes; workspace.cjs:16 launches node /app/server.js with env-only PATH/HOME/NODE_PATH/PORT=3000/DB_PATH=/tmp/hireops-workspace.db and cwd /tmp; results/workspace.json has 0 failed results and page_errors [] including 'restart keeps jobs, cards, order, messages and activity without reseeding'; server.log shows two '[hireops] listening on 3000' (initial + restart). Adversarial: a plausible broken reference (seed read from /assets or cwd-relative public dir, or health behind DB init) would fail under test.sh's /tmp cwd / unprivileged copy - this reference avoids each. A conforming alternative submission (no DB reset logic, DB at DB_PATH) is unaffected by anything in solve.sh, which grades nothing. Limitation (not a defect for this row): the evidence index records no log of solve.sh itself executing in the agent image (how /app was populated for the scripted run is not recorded), and there is no Oracle/configured-judge result; I ran no Docker. The solve.sh logic is simple and statically sound, so this is a Note-level gap, not a blocker; no Oracle score is implied.
